item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00368","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C20","C07","C15"],"selected_candidate_label":"C20","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C20 is the immediately preceding Flag Day proclamation and supplies the child’s concrete drafting structure and much of its operative language: the same congressional resolution, direction to display the flag on all Government buildings on June 14, appeal for public observance and home display, and concluding reflection on privileges, obligations, and rededication. C07 and C15 share the same annual form and machinery, but C20 is closest in language and sequence.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"Whereas the Congress, by a joint resolution approved August 3, 1949 (63 Stat. 492), designated June 14 of each year as Flag Day and requested the President to issue annually a proclamation calling for its observance","parent_excerpt":"Whereas the Congress, by a joint resolution approved August 3, 1949 (63 Stat. 492), has designated June 14 of each year as Flag Day","explanation":"Both use the same resolution and annual Flag Day designation as the final recital supporting the proclamation."},{"child_excerpt":"do hereby direct that the flag be displayed on all Government buildings on Sunday, June 14, 1953, and I call upon all our people to observe the day with appropriate ceremonies","parent_excerpt":"do hereby direct that the flag be displayed on all Government buildings on Saturday, June 14, 1952, and I call upon the people of the Nation to observe that day by suitable ceremonies","explanation":"This is a close year-and-weekday substitution within the same operative sentence."},{"child_excerpt":"Let us display the flag proudly at our homes and other suitable places","parent_excerpt":"including the display of the flag at their homes and other appropriate places","explanation":"The child preserves the parent’s request for private display at homes and comparable locations."},{"child_excerpt":"giving solemn thought to the inestimable privileges ... and ... corresponding obligations ... and let us rededicate ourselves","parent_excerpt":"give special thought on Flag Day not only to their many rights and privileges but also to their duties and responsibilities ... to the end that we may rededicate ourselves","explanation":"The child closely adapts C20’s distinctive closing progression from reflection on privileges and duties to collective rededication."}]}
